headline: The one memory this review flags -- `m02`, which states both halves of k4's defect in the same two clauses as the fix's own rationale comment -- is a memory the fix-locality scan shows NOTHING for, on k4 or on any task. Every identifier in it predates the fix, and the four words it shares with k4's changed lines (`invocation`, `option`, `order`, `parameters`) are English prose from an added docstring, which is why they are excluded. Meanwhile the scan's own hits are `close`, `flag_value`, `is_flag`, `default`, `value`, `UNSET` and `click` -- the working vocabulary of every memory about option handling, on-subject and off. So on this task set the scan flags memories the reading clears and clears the memory the reading flags. That is the concrete form of the general claim that identifier scans cannot establish semantic leakage, and it is why the conclusion rests on reading.
